newsitem.title: CHINA: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.
newsitem.headline: Shanghai T-bill repo rates end up, spots down.

text.p: Contracts on the treasury bill repurchase market in Shanghai closed mostly up on Monday due to a strong rally on the domestic A share markets, traders said.
The annual rate for the most actively traded three-day contract rose to 6.50 percent from 3.99 percent last Friday.
The latest-maturing 182-day contract was the only loser.
Total turnover of the six-contract market soared to 4.8 million lots from 1.9 million lots.
One lot is 1,000 yuan face value of treasury bills.
Share prices on the Shanghai and Shenzhen stock exchanges surged around three percent on average on Monday, boosting fund demand on the repo market, traders said.
"Institutions borrowed heavily, especially in the three-day and seven-day contracts, to trade on the A share markets," said one trader.
A new A share issue on the Shenzhen stock exchange also helped to push up the repo rates and turnover, traders said.
Repo rate movements in the next few days would largely depend on the performance of the A share markets, traders said.
Contracts on the T-bill spot market in Shanghai ended mostly down on an expected technical correction after sharp gains in the past two weeks, traders said.
The most actively traded 10-year bond that matures in June 2006 fell sharply to 111.16 yuan from 112.00 yuan.
Combined volume of the eight-contract market fell slightly to 1.04 million lots from 1.14 million lots.
Traders said the rise on the A share markets was another factor pulling down the spot contracts on Monday.
Traders said they expected the contracts to move around the current level in the next few days.
